citeAs: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang (2025). WebWalker: Benchmarking LLMs in Web Traversal. arXiv:2501.07572.
creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang (Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group)
description: WebWalkerQA is a benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs on their ability to perform web traversal, specifically their capacity to traverse a website's subpages to extract high-quality data systematically. It comprises 680 question-answer pairs from four real-world domains (conference, organization, education, and game) across over 1373 webpages, including both single-source and multi-source QA types in English and Chinese.
name: WebWalkerQA
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Crowd-sourced human annotation (platform not specified); GPT-4o used for initial LLM-based annotation
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A two-stage annotation process was used: (1) LLM-based annotation: GPT-4o traversed official websites, constructed queries based on page information, and verified/filtered QA pairs to retain only those with short answers containing entities. (2) Human annotation: crowd-sourced human annotators rewrote and calibrated questions and answers to ensure correctness and consistency. Specific prompts were used for multi-source and single-source data annotation, including question generation and question-answer verification steps.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is constrained to four specific domains (conference, organization, education, and game) and focuses on official websites with structured clickable content. The multi-source QA tasks were specifically designed so they cannot be easily exploited by search engine shortcuts. The dataset is bilingual (Chinese and English) to reflect real-world web environments.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected using a two-stage funnel annotation strategy. First, official websites were traversed recursively to collect sublinks and page information. GPT-4o performed initial annotation to generate synthetic QA pairs. Then crowd-sourced human annotators conducted quality control and filtering. Root pages were identified via Google search using keywords like "conference official website" or "game official website", followed by manual filtering.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of official websites' subpages and their content, collected by recursively traversing websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains. Web page content was extracted in Markdown-like format using the ai4crawl tool, along with clickable HTML buttons and corresponding URLs extracted using Beautiful Soup.
rai:dataLimitations: Dataset size is limited to 680 high-quality QA pairs due to the complexity of queries. The dataset only uses HTML-DOM to parse clickable buttons and does not incorporate visual modalities such as screenshots. WebWalker is driven by prompting without additional training.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries were verified and filtered to retain only QA pairs with short answers containing entities, and those deviating from natural, human-like phrasing were removed. Web page content was parsed into Markdown-like format using ai4crawl, and clickable HTML buttons with corresponding URLs were extracted using Beautiful Soup.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark highlights the importance of deep, vertical exploration in web-based tasks, paving the way for more scalable and reliable LLM-based information retrieval integrated with RAG. It addresses the limitation of traditional search engines that retrieve only shallow content, enabling LLMs to handle complex, multi-layered information from authoritative official sources.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking LLMs on web traversal tasks; evaluating the capacity of LLMs to traverse website subpages to extract high-quality data; evaluating RAG systems on deep information retrieval; training data for agent tuning (approximately 14k silver QA pairs available as supplementary training data).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o was used for initial LLM-based annotation to generate synthetic QA pairs and verify/filter them. GPT-4 was used as the evaluator to determine correctness of responses by comparing predicted answers with ground truth using CoT prompting.

evidence.description: We construct a challenging benchmark, WebWalkerQA, which is composed of 680 queries from four real-world scenarios across over 1373 webpages.

evidence.inLanguage: WebWalkerQA is a bilingual dataset that includes both Chinese and English, reflecting the most widely used and universal languages in real-world web environments.

evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: We utilize the web page's markdown content along with clickable HTML buttons (and corresponding URL) extracted using Beautiful Soup as the observation for the current page.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human Annotation After the synthetic queries are generated by LLM, human annotators can rewrite and calibrate the questions and answers to ensure the QA pairs are correct and consistent.

We use GPT-4 as the evaluator, which determines the correctness of responses by comparing the predicted answer with the ground truth using CoT prompting strategy.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Step3: Verify and filter for legitimate queries that deviate from natural, human-like phrasing, retaining only QA pairs with short answers containing entities.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: WebWalkerQA, designed specifically to evaluate LLMs on their ability to handle queries embedded in complex, multi-step web interactions on a given root website. Additionally, we possess a collection of approximately 14k silver QA pairs, which, although not yet carefully human-verified, can serve as supplementary training data to enhance agent performance.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset Size: Due to the complexity of queries in the web-agent domain, similar to benchmarks such as AssistantBench (Yoran et al., 2024) (214) and MMIna (Zhang et al., 2024c) (1,050), GAIA (Mialon et al., 2024) (466), our proposed WebWalkerQA currently comprises 680 high-quality QA pairs. Multimodal Environment: In this work, we only utilize HTML-DOM to parse clickable buttons.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: Our work highlights the importance of deep, vertical exploration in web-based tasks, paving the way for more scalable and reliable LLM-based information retrieval integrated with RAG.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: These domains are selected because they provide authoritative information relevant to their respective fields, and their pages contain rich clickable content, offering substantial depth for exploration. Notably, the multi-source QA tasks can not be easily exploited by search engine shortcuts.
